domain: Making chips and film from Mercury and refreshing the fleet, 2045-2300+: fab throughput, H/C/N/F/Cl-free process chemistry, free vacuum and cold, energy per kg, design for manufacture, and generational refresh
summary: MANUFACTURING AND REFRESH. (1) Fab throughput, not Mercury mass, is the first wall. At the heat-wall export (3.94e19 kg/yr) the swarm needs 9.9e17-3.9e18 m2/yr of leading-edge-equivalent die = 1.6e19-6.2e19 300 mm wafers/yr: 8.7e10-3.4e11x today's entire output (1.8e8/yr; the prompt's "30 M" is per month in 200 mm-eq) and 1.3e12-5.2e12x the <=7 nm output. A 2026 fab holds ~250 kg of tools per m2/yr of die (110-500, two derivations); at that productivity the fab stock would be 6-25 yr of export and the doubling time x5-18. Keeping T_d <= 1.25 yr needs <=3.6-14 kg per m2/yr of leading-edge-equivalent die (17-69x better). Only an area-parallel process at near-leading-edge density gets there: panel imprint + inorganic self-assembly (9-15 nm, speculative; T_d x1.16 in 2040, x1.23-1.26 later with right-sized NVM). Roll-to-roll imprint is cheap per m2 but its 50-100 nm devices need ~50x the area and ~30x the J/op; a space-native EUV/FEL wafer fab (8-12 nm) costs T_d x1.7-3.8; high-NA EUV buys resolution, not throughput. Adiabatic film logic is unmanufacturable (die = 21-86 % of film area). (2) Chemistry: H is the only hard wall (~5e13 kg; wet processing would use 1.25e22 kg/yr, organic resist >=5.8e14). C (1.1e18 kg/yr), Cl (1.1e17) and S come up with the rock. Use MOE/metallothermic Si, a Cl + Zn/Mg SiCl4 loop for 9N Si, Cl2 etch, O2, PVD oxides and resistless/inorganic patterning; no water, organics, N or F. (3) Free vacuum cuts fab electricity ~60 %. (4) Energy: 1,150 MJ/kg (2026, space fab; 2,710 at terrestrial intensity), 1,030-1,250 MJ/kg in 2040-2100+ with NVM right-sized (up to 5,180 with 32 GB chiplets): 4-20x the model's 255, chips 80-95 % of it, yet only 3-5 % of swarm power. Factories must leave Mercury by model year ~37. (5) Older nodes lose twice (10x J/op and 10x area); the film beats HBM pods on capital only below ~110-190 kg per m2/yr (270-320 with NVM right-sized). Node target: Earth imports (seed), imprint+DSA or space leading edge (growth), leading edge after the wall. (6) Refresh by sail: re-skin on reused frames, recycle in orbit (rho ~0.94; 13-25 MJ/kg to recover feedstock). B_ss = D L/(1-rho): 10-yr lives without recycling cap the swarm at 0.57 % (1 % never reached); rho 0.94 gives 9.5-25 % (90 % of it by ~2466); 10 % needs rho >= 0.945 (2026 mix) or 0.854 (2100+ mix). Replacement share: 0.1 % pre-wall, ~50 % by 2106, 86 % by 2150, 98 % by 2300.

patterning_technologies.name: EUV wafer fab, terrestrial 2026 (N3/N2)
patterning_technologies.notes: ~25 EUV + ~40 DUV layers, ~1,000+ steps; LPP source needs flowing H2 and Sn; wet cleans, UPW, organic resist, F/N chemistry.

patterning_technologies.name: High-NA EUV wafer fab (EXE:5200B class, 0.55 NA)
patterning_technologies.notes: 8 nm resolution, 175 wph at 50 mJ/cm2, ~1.4 MW per tool; replaces EUV double patterning, so fab-level intensity stays ~leading-edge. Buys resolution, not area throughput.

patterning_technologies.name: Space-native wafer fab: dry vacuum processing, shared FEL-EUV, 450 mm / panels, no building/HVAC/UPW
patterning_technologies.notes: Removes building, cleanroom air, UPW, abatement and most pumps (~half of terrestrial facility mass and 50-65 % of energy); stages and optics still heavy.

patterning_technologies.name: DUV-immersion multipatterning fab (N7-class, no EUV)
patterning_technologies.notes: SAQP needs more deposition/etch steps; N7 wafer ~half the N3 price per area, 2.5-3x the area per function.

patterning_technologies.name: Mature-node fab (28 nm class, single-patterned ArF)
patterning_technologies.notes: ~30-35 masks; wafer ~1/7 of N3 per area; 6x SRAM area and ~10-19x logic area per function vs N3.

patterning_technologies.name: Wafer nanoimprint (Canon FPA-1200NZ2C class)
patterning_technologies.notes: Replaces the scanner, not the rest of the fab: wafer-level productivity per layer is similar to EUV; resist is organic.

patterning_technologies.name: Panel/plate imprint + directed self-assembly pitch division, dry vacuum line
patterning_technologies.notes: Coarse imprinted guides (~90 nm pitch) multiplied 4-5x by self-assembly (18 nm pitch shown on a 193i guide); needs an inorganic (H-free) self-assembling system and self-aligned design rules for poor overlay.

patterning_technologies.name: Roll-to-roll nanoimprint web line
patterning_technologies.notes: One 250 mm station patterns 3.6e+06 m2/yr; overlay is micrometre-class, so devices must be self-aligned.
patterning_technologies.evidence_class: demonstrated (100 nm at 30 m/min, pilot) / speculation (full device flow)

patterning_technologies.name: Vacuum web coater (unpatterned deposition step, TopMet class)
patterning_technologies.notes: 2.6e+09 m2/yr per coater: deposition is never the bottleneck.

patterning_technologies.name: Multi-beam e-beam direct write (IMS MBMW class)
patterning_technologies.notes: 10 m2/yr per tool: only for masters, templates and masks (one master seeds ~1e5-1e6 imprint copies).

patterning_technologies.name: Scanning-probe atomically precise patterning (H-depassivation lithography)
patterning_technologies.notes: 2.3e-10 m2/yr per tip: 1e20+ x too slow; needs H as the resist.

patterning_technologies.name: Molecular manufacturing (convergent-assembly nanofactory)
patterning_technologies.notes: Theoretical design (diamondoid, i.e. carbon-based): 10 kg unit, 1.3 kg/h, self-duplication in ~15 h. No demonstration.

world_output_2025.note: The prompt quoted ~30 M 300-mm wafers/yr in total. SEMI gives 33.6 M wafers PER MONTH (200 mm-equivalent) in 2025 = 1.79e+08 300-mm-equivalent wafers/yr; the leading edge (<=7 nm) is 1.18e+07 wafers/yr.

tool_intensity_derivation_2026.evidence_class: demonstrated inputs (tool throughput, mass, WFE) + estimate (capex shares, $/kg)

chemistry.today: Carbothermic arc furnace (coke, coal, graphite electrodes): ~0.86 kg C per kg Si; 12 kWh/kg
chemistry.mercury: (a) Molten-oxide electrolysis of the silicate melt with an inert anode: O2 at the anode, Fe then Si at the cathode, leaving an Fe-free Mg-Ca-Al-silicate melt that becomes cover glass and enamel. (b) Metallothermic: SiO2 + 2Mg -> Si + 2MgO, Mg regenerated electrolytically. (c) Carbothermic with crustal graphite and a closed CO -> C loop (Boudouard + solid-oxide CO2 electrolysis).
chemistry.limits: Thermodynamic floor 32.4 MJ/kg Si (dHf SiO2 -910.7 kJ/mol). MOE is lab-scale (1600 C, inert anodes of Ir/Cr-alloys are the open problem). Route (c) needs >=85 % C recycling to live on the carbon that the mines bring up.
chemistry.evidence: demonstrated (lab MOE, magnesiothermic) / speculation (closed C loop at scale)

chemistry.today: Siemens trichlorosilane + H2 CVD (HCl, H2): 52-64 kWh/kg; or UMG with H2O-plasma B removal
chemistry.mercury: Vacuum metallurgy in free vacuum: directional solidification (metals, k<<1), electron-beam melting (P, Al, Ca evaporate), O2-plasma / CaO-SiO2 slag for boron (no H2O), and simply choosing low-B feed (Mercury primitive-mantle B ~0.3 ppm).
chemistry.limits: B (k=0.8) and P (k=0.35) do not segregate; EB removes P 25 -> <0.1 ppmw in 1.2 h; B removal without H is the least proven step.

chemistry.today: Siemens process (HCl, H2, SiHCl3) + Cz pulling in Ar; EG poly 92-124 kWh/kg
chemistry.mercury: Chloride route without H: Cl2 + MG-Si -> SiCl4; fractional distillation (BCl3 bp 12.5 C, PCl3 76 C vs SiCl4 57.6 C); reduce with Zn or Mg vapour (DuPont 1949 Zn process, Kroll-type MgCl2 loop); float-zone refine and grow crystals in free vacuum.
chemistry.limits: Cl inventory: 2.3e+16 kg in process at the 2026-basis heat wall (0.0022 of crust Cl); losses must stay <=1e-3 per pass (then 0.025 of the Cl that the mines bring up).
chemistry.evidence: demonstrated (historical Zn-SiCl4 hyper-pure Si; Kroll Mg-Cl loop for Ti)

chemistry.today: Cz ingot + diamond-wire sawing (water/glycol coolant, ~57 um kerf) to 130-160 um wafers
chemistry.mercury: Kerfless: high-rate e-beam evaporation of Si (1-18 um/min demonstrated) onto the glass cover or a release layer, then line-laser liquid-phase crystallisation; or horizontal ribbon growth from a melt in vacuum.
chemistry.limits: LPC cells reached ~13 %, far from the 20-22.5 % AM0 assumed; grain boundaries need passivation (H) or large grains.
chemistry.evidence: demonstrated (CSG LPC, e-beam rates) / speculation (20 % cells without H)

chemistry.mercury: Molecular-beam / e-beam evaporation in free vacuum (orbital MBE shown by the Wake Shield Facility); SiCl4 + Zn CVD where conformality matters.
chemistry.limits: Line-of-sight deposition: poor step coverage; conformal layers need chloride CVD or reflow.

chemistry.today: Wet/dry oxidation, Si3N4 (NH3+SiH4), SiNx:H and a-Si:H passivation, SiCOH low-k, ALD Al2O3 (TMA + H2O)
chemistry.mercury: Dry O2 oxidation (O2 is the reduction by-product: 9.5e+18 kg/yr at the heat wall); PVD Al2O3/MgO/ZrO2 with negative fixed charge for field-effect passivation; porous SiO2 or vacuum gaps for low-k; trace-H anneals with cryo-recapture.
chemistry.limits: a-Si:H layers would use 2.1e+13 kg H/yr (ice+regolith stock lasts 2.3 yr). A 1e13 cm-2 trace-H anneal uses 4e+10 kg/yr (2.1 of an even 250-yr share of the stock at 10x net loss). No nitrides (no N).
chemistry.evidence: demonstrated (dry oxide, PVD Al2O3) / speculation (H-free passivation reaching 20 % cells)

chemistry.process: High-k / metal gate and memory oxides
chemistry.today: HfO2 by ALD (HfCl4/TEMAH + H2O), TiN/TaN (N), W fill (WF6)
chemistry.mercury: ZrO2 / Zr-rich ferroelectrics and Al2O3 by atomic-layer MBE (metal flux + O atoms) or chloride precursors + O3; NiSi/CoSi2 FUSI gates; Mo-free, W-free, N-free stacks.
chemistry.limits: Hf, W, Ru, Pt, In, Te are scarce (study 2); nitride barriers and work-function metals need redesign.
chemistry.evidence: roadmap (ZrO2 ferroelectrics, silicide gates) / speculation (H-free atomic-layer MBE at scale)

chemistry.today: Chemically amplified organic resists, solvents (PGMEA), TMAH developer (C, H, N); EUV metal-oxide resists are organometallic
chemistry.mercury: Resistless or inorganic: imprint directly into softened glass / sol-free oxides; stencil (shadow-mask) deposition through Si membranes in UHV; self-developing inorganic resists (radiolytic metal oxides/halides, e.g. NaCl-type); direct-write e-beam/ion only for masters.
chemistry.limits: Organic resist would need 5.8e+14 kg H/yr even with 100 % deposition efficiency (ice+regolith lasts 0.083 yr; closure 0.9997 required); carbon is NOT the limit (0.0046 of the C the mines bring up).
chemistry.evidence: demonstrated (stencil lithography, NIL into inorganics at lab scale) / speculation (production)

chemistry.today: Fluorocarbons, SF6, NF3 (F, C, N); Cl2/HBr (Br); BCl3
chemistry.mercury: Cl2 plasma and atomic-layer etch for Si and Al (Cl from regolith, recaptured by cryo-condensation of SiCl4/AlCl3/Cl2 on cold panels and electrolysis of chlorides); SiO2 removed by the UHV reaction SiO2 + Si -> 2 SiO(g) or avoided by additive patterning; O2+/Mg+ ion milling.
chemistry.limits: Cl2 etch circulates 2.6e+17 kg Cl/yr; 1 % loss = 0.024 of the Cl the mines bring up. No F-based oxide etch (F unmeasured).
chemistry.evidence: demonstrated (Cl2 RIE/ALE; oxide desorption in MBE) / speculation (F-free full flow)

chemistry.today: RCA/SPM/HF wet cleans; ~7 m3 water per 300 mm wafer (2-3 Mgal/day at 40k wpm)
chemistry.mercury: Dry cleans in vacuum: thermal flash, O-atom/UV oxidation, low-energy ion sputter, electrostatic particle control; no airborne particles in vacuum.
chemistry.limits: Wet processing would need 1.3e+22 kg H/yr: Mercury's ice+regolith lasts 3.9e-09 yr (closure 1-2e-11 impossible).
chemistry.evidence: physics floor (H budget) + demonstrated (UHV surface prep)

chemistry.today: Silica/ceria slurries in water with organics
chemistry.mercury: Subtractive Al/Cl2 metal patterning (pre-1997 flow) with glass reflow and gas-cluster/ion-beam planarisation; fewer metal levels on 0.15 W film chiplets.
chemistry.limits: Limits wiring density to ~6-8 levels; pushes chiplets toward SRAM/NVM-friendly, wire-light designs.

chemistry.today: Cu electroplating (aqueous), Ta/TaN barriers, W contacts, Co/Ru liners
chemistry.mercury: Evaporated/sputtered Al(Si) and Mg-Al, NiSi/CoSi2 contacts, Co lines at the finest pitches (Co from the core is abundant).
chemistry.limits: Mercury Cu ~2.4e18 kg in silicates vs 4.1e18 kg full-swarm demand; W impossible (project pass 1).

chemistry.today: Implant from BF3, PH3, AsH3, B2H6; POCl3 diffusion
chemistry.mercury: Solid-source ion implantation (evaporated/sputtered P, B, Al), in-situ doping during e-beam epitaxy, Al-alloyed p+ contacts.
chemistry.limits: As/Sb scarce; B needs to be separated from feed (BCl3 distillation gives it as a by-product).

chemistry.today: Organic substrates, epoxy underfill, Sn-Ag-Cu solder, elastomer stamps for mass transfer
chemistry.mercury: Oxide-oxide / Al-Al direct bonding onto the film, enamel overcoat (design spec), parallel electrostatic or laser-release transfer from glass carriers: 5.2e+15 placements/s at the 2026-basis heat wall.
chemistry.limits: Pick-and-place at ~10/s per head would need ~5e14 heads; only parallel transfer (~1e2-1e3 dies per cycle) or monolithic film logic scales.
chemistry.evidence: demonstrated (hybrid bonding, micro-LED mass transfer) / speculation (H-free transfer)

chemistry.today: N2, Ar, He, clean dry air, H2; turbo/dry pumps in a pressurised cleanroom
chemistry.mercury: Free vacuum (Mercury exosphere <=1e12 m-3, interplanetary better); reagents recovered by cryo-panels behind sunshades; O2 from refining.
chemistry.limits: Outgassing of the fab itself sets local pressure; Cl/S/O must be trapped, not vented, to stay inside the volatile budget.

chemistry.today: Laser-produced Sn plasma, CO2 drive laser (C, N2, He), flowing H2 buffer for collector protection
chemistry.mercury: Electron-accelerator FEL (ERL) at 13.5 nm feeding many scanners: no Sn, no CO2 laser, no H2 buffer.
chemistry.limits: ERL-FEL is a design study (>10 kW, 800 MeV, ~10 mA).

how_far_they_stretch_2026_basis_heat_wal.carbothermic_PV_Si: C circulating 7.1e+18 kg/yr; mined C covers it with >=85 % CO->C recycling
how_far_they_stretch_2026_basis_heat_wal.O2: by-product 9.5e+18 kg/yr from absorber Si alone: oxidation and plasma O are free

volatiles_budget.verdict: Hydrogen is the only hard wall: Mercury's ~5e13 kg (3e12-2e14) of H is 1e-9 yr of terrestrial wet processing and <0.1 yr of organic resist. Carbon is not scarce while mining the crust (1.1e18 kg/yr comes up with the rock at the heat wall), chlorine is a usable working fluid (1e19 kg in the crust, 1.1e17 kg/yr mined), sulfur and sodium are abundant, N and F must be designed out. So: dry, resistless/inorganic, chloride-and-oxygen process chemistry; H only as a recaptured trace; no water.
volatiles_budget.evidence_class: demonstrated (MESSENGER abundances) + model (demands) + speculation (regolith H, depth of C)

free_vacuum_and_cold.notes: Free vacuum removes cleanroom air handling, UPW, purge gases, most pumping and abatement: ~60 % (48-71 %) of fab electricity and 30-50 % of equipment mass plus the building. Free cold is weaker near Mercury (9 kW/m2 sunlight): radiators must be edge-on or shaded; cryo-panels at 40-80 K behind multilayer shades recapture Cl, SiCl4, O2 and S instead of venting. Film processing barely benefits (it is enthalpy-bound: reduction, evaporation, melting).

node_target_by_era.film_chiplets: Imported from Earth: leading edge (N2/A14-class, ~10 nm half-pitch). Mercury makes the film, glass, Mg and coarse power/control electronics (45-100 nm class).
node_target_by_era.why: Earth's entire 2025 leading-edge output (6.7e+05 m2/yr of good die) is 1.7e+10 W/yr of film chiplets = 1.6e+07 kg/yr of sails: it carries only the first ~4.5 doublings (6.1-6.8 if Earth triples-quintuples LE capacity by 2045). A 1e6 kg seed cannot hold even one 2026-style leading-edge fab (~3e7 kg of tools).

node_target_by_era.film_chiplets: Panel/plate imprint + inorganic directed self-assembly, self-aligned, ~9-15 nm half-pitch (J/op x2 vs leading edge) if it can be made to work; fallback: space-native leading-edge wafer fab (8-12 nm, J/op x1).
node_target_by_era.why: Doubling-time multipliers (2040 devices): panel imprint+DSA x1.16, space-native leading edge x1.7, terrestrial-style leading edge x5.37, DUV multipatterning x7.05, 28 nm class x7.02. Older nodes lose twice: 10x the J/op AND 10x the area, so 7x slower growth. Compute at model year 60: panel 1.6e+37 FLOP/s vs space leading edge 3.9e+33.

node_target_by_era.film_chiplets: Leading edge for every new and refreshed sail (~6-10 nm half-pitch, 2D-channel CFET-class); right-size NVM to the useful minimum (0.9-1.65 GB per chiplet).
node_target_by_era.why: Mass now binds, so FLOP/s per kg = 1/(J/op x g/W) decides: the leading edge gives 2x the compute of imprint+DSA chips per kg of Mercury. Fab stock/fleet = I a / L: 0.397 (space leading edge, 2100+ planned memory) -> 0.165 with right-sized memory; pushing I below ~15 keeps fabs <10 % of the fleet. Refresh the 2060-2095 imprint-era sails first (they gain the most).

node_target_by_era.film_chiplets: Physics-limited irreversible CMOS (~5-8 nm half-pitch; within ~2x of the ~7e-16 J/op practical floor). Adiabatic film logic only if a <=20 nm web/panel process reaches <=0.1-0.35 kg of tools per m2/yr.
node_target_by_era.why: Adiabatic logic needs 0.862 of the film area as die (2100+) and 84100.0 MJ/kg with a space wafer fab; no demonstrated or plausible wafer-fab class meets the tool intensity it needs (0.0909).

refresh.strategy: Refresh by SAIL, recycle in the swarm shell. A depot craft brings two new film rolls (with chips) and swaps them onto the existing hub cradles, booms and vanes ("re-skin", 94 % of sail mass replaced); the old film is rolled up and recycled at co-orbiting depots. Pods swap only their 0.8 g/W compute modules (20 % of pod mass) and keep wings, radiators and loops for 2-3 generations. Chiplet-level swap is impractical (1.06e8 enamel-overcoated dies per sail, ~2,900 head-hours each). A separable rear "compute laminate" (31 % of film mass) is a speculative upgrade. Never return material to Mercury: ~17 km/s and 35 % propellant at Isp 4,000 s, and it would re-enter the 5e18 W heat budget.

chiplet_swap.verdict: impractical: enamel-overcoated flip-chip dies, 1e8 per sail, ~3,000 head-hours per sail; parallel transfer only works at manufacture

recovery_fraction.losses: dead/uncontrollable sails 1-3 %, transfer propellant 0.3-3 %, meteoroid ablation

recycle_energy.where: in orbit (swarm-shell depots); Mercury return rejected
recycle_energy.evidence_class: demonstrated (terrestrial recycling yields, Mg distillation) + speculation (in-orbit depots)

replacement_share_by_era.rule: During exponential growth replacement is 2^(-L/T_d) of output (0.1 % at L = 10, T_d = 1). After the heat wall it climbs to ~50 % within one life and >85 % within a century.

steady_state.formula: B_ss = D_cap L / (1 - rho); D_cap = 3.94e19 kg/yr; all output is refresh at B_ss
steady_state.headline: With 10-yr lives and no recycling the fleet saturates at 3.9e20 kg (0.57 % coverage at the 2026 mix): the model's 1 % swarm (year 62) is never reached. With 94 % in-orbit recycling B_ss = 6.6e21 kg (9.5 % coverage, 2026 mix; 25 % with the lighter 2100+ mix), 90 % of it by model year 416.0 (~2466). 10 % coverage needs rho >= 0.945 (2026 mix) or >= 0.854 (2100+ mix) at L = 10, or rho >= 0.89 at L = 20. Mercury's rock limit (4e22 kg) needs rho >= 0.99.
steady_state.rock_exhaustion: cumulative delivery reaches the 4e22 kg rock limit ~1,000 yr after the heat wall (calendar ~3100); after that rho < 1 makes the fleet decay at (1-rho)/L = 0.6 %/yr unless core metal is used

economic_refresh_age.rule: If Mercury mass binds and fabs are ample, refresh a sail when (1 - (1+g)^-a)/(1 - rho) > 1, i.e. a* = ln(1/rho)/ln(1+g), g = yearly J/op gain. If fabs bind, refresh only at physical end of life (20-30 yr: PV keeps 92 % after 10 yr).
economic_refresh_age.recommendation: L = 10 yr through ~2150 (g 2-5 %/yr, fabs still binding); 15-20 yr after ~2150 as g falls below ~1 %/yr and fab stock (I a / L) must stay small.

growth_curve_change.exponential_phase: unchanged except T_d -> T_d (1 + I a / kappa): x1.16 (imprint+DSA) to x1.7 (space leading edge) with 2040 chips; x5.4 with 2026-style fabs
growth_curve_change.post_heat_wall: replace linear growth by B(t) = B_ss - (B_ss - B_cap) exp(-(1-rho)(t - t_cap)/L) (within 4 % of the cohort simulation)
growth_curve_change.visual: the curve bends over after ~2096 and approaches a ceiling; coverage keeps creeping up as lighter generations replace heavier ones (same kg, more m2)

refresh.evidence_class: model (cohort simulation, project growth rule) + speculation (lives, recovery fractions)

architecture_implications.question: Does any fab model scale to the heat-wall build rate?
architecture_implications.answer: No terrestrial-style fab does. The build needs 9e10-3e11x today's whole wafer output; at 2026 tool productivity the fab equipment alone would weigh 6-25 years of the export stream and stretch the doubling time 5-18x.
architecture_implications.numbers: Die area at the wall: 9.92e+17 m2/yr (2026) to 3.91e+18 (2100+); EUV-style flow needs 230000000000000.0 scanners (4.36e+19 kg) in 2026. Required tool intensity for T_d x1.25: 14.3 -> 3.64 kg per m2/yr, i.e. 17.4x-68.8x better than 2026 (250.0).

architecture_implications.question: What feature size is achievable at that scale?
architecture_implications.answer: Area-parallel patterning sets it: ~50-100 nm with roll-to-roll imprint (demonstrated pattern scale), ~9-15 nm only if imprinted guides plus inorganic self-assembly work on panels (speculative), 8-12 nm with space-native wafer fabs at a 1.7-3.8x doubling-time cost. Multi-beam e-beam and probe lithography are 3-12 orders of magnitude too slow and serve only for masters.
architecture_implications.numbers: Tool intensity per layer: EUV 1.7, R2R imprint 0.0014-0.0056, vacuum web coater 2e-5-6e-5, multi-beam 1,900-4,800, H-depassivation 4e12 kg per m2/yr.

architecture_implications.question: Does manufacturing favour distributed film or concentrated pods?
architecture_implications.answer: Film, provided fab productivity improves ~2x beyond today and film NVM is right-sized. Film chiplets need 7-10x more die area per W than HBM pods, so at today's 250 kg per m2/yr pods need less total capital while growth is capital-limited; after the heat wall Mercury mass binds and the film wins again (0.5-0.9 vs 4 g/W).
architecture_implications.numbers: Break-even tool intensity: 117.0 (2026), 186.0 (2040), 143.0 (2070), 110.0 (2100+) kg per m2/yr; with right-sized NVM 267.0-316.0.

architecture_implications.question: Are older nodes fine because film area is cheap?
architecture_implications.answer: No. Area is cheap for the film but not for the fab: an older node costs ~10x the J/op AND ~10x the patterned area per function, so it is worse in both regimes. What helps is a process with far more area per kg of tool, at whatever feature size it reaches.
architecture_implications.numbers: 28 nm class: J x10, area x10, T_d x7.02 (2040 devices) vs x1.7 for a space leading-edge fab; DUV multipatterning x7.05.

architecture_implications.question: Memory sizing
architecture_implications.answer: Size film NVM to the useful minimum (0.23/0.9/1.65 GB per chiplet), not the 1/8/32 GB that study 2 shows is possible: capacity beyond it costs fab output, not mass.
architecture_implications.numbers: LEA die per W 30.7/40/52 -> 22.5/22.2/21.6 mm2/W; T_d multiplier (panel class, 2100+) 1.62 -> 1.26; energy per kg 2100+ 5180.0 -> 1250.0 MJ/kg.

architecture_implications.question: Adiabatic logic (study 1)
architecture_implications.answer: Not manufacturable on the film with any wafer-fab class: the die becomes 21 % (2070) to 86 % (2100+) of the film area. It needs a web-speed process at <=20 nm, which does not exist.
architecture_implications.numbers: Required tool intensity 0.348 (2070) / 0.0909 (2100+) kg per m2/yr; energy 24300.0 / 84100.0 MJ/kg with a space wafer fab.

architecture_implications.question: Where do the factories go?
architecture_implications.answer: Mercury is a quarry and catapult. Refineries and fabs work on the surface only until model year ~37; after that they must sit in Mercury co-orbit, with refresh depots in the swarm shell.
architecture_implications.numbers: Processing heat 1.44e+21 W at the 2026-basis wall (3 % of swarm output) vs a 5e18 W surface cap; radiators 1.09e+18 m2 (320 K fab, 1,000 K refinery).

architecture_implications.question: Chemistry
architecture_implications.answer: Dry, vacuum, chloride-and-oxygen process chemistry: MOE or metallothermic Si for PV, a Cl/Zn-or-Mg loop with SiCl4 distillation for 9N chip Si, Cl2 etch, O2 oxidation, PVD oxides, resistless or inorganic patterning. No water, no organics, no nitrides, no fluorine; H only as a recaptured trace.
architecture_implications.numbers: See volatiles_budget: H stock ~5e13 kg vs 1.25e22 kg/yr for wet processing; Cl 1.1e17 kg/yr arrives with the rock.

architecture_implications.question: Placement
architecture_implications.answer: Chiplet placement becomes a top-level manufacturing problem: 5e15-1.6e16 dies per second at the wall. Use parallel transfer from glass carriers or monolithic logic in the film's c-Si; keep the 0.15 W chiplet (the P^2 spreader rule forbids fewer, bigger dies).
architecture_implications.numbers: 1,551-2,730 sites per m2 x 1.2e20-2e20 m2/yr of film.

architecture_implications.question: Refresh and the size of the swarm
architecture_implications.answer: Service life and in-orbit recycling, not the heat wall alone, set the final swarm. 10-yr lives without recycling cap it at 0.57 % coverage; 94 % recycling gives 9.5-25 %; the rock-limited swarm needs 99 %.
architecture_implications.numbers: With 10-yr lives and no recycling the fleet saturates at 3.9e20 kg (0.57 % coverage at the 2026 mix): the model's 1 % swarm (year 62) is never reached. With 94 % in-orbit recycling B_ss = 6.6e21 kg (9.5 % coverage, 2026 mix; 25 % with the lighter 2100+ mix), 90 % of it by model year 416.0 (~2466). 10 % coverage needs rho >= 0.945 (2026 mix) or >= 0.854 (2100+ mix) at L = 10, or rho >= 0.89 at L = 20. Mercury's rock limit (4e22 kg) needs rho >= 0.99.

architecture_implications.question: Seed era
architecture_implications.answer: The first ~4-7 doublings run on chips imported from Earth; Mercury-made chiplets must take over by a built mass of ~1e8 kg.
architecture_implications.numbers: Earth's entire 2025 leading-edge output (6.7e+05 m2/yr of good die) is 1.7e+10 W/yr of film chiplets = 1.6e+07 kg/yr of sails: it carries only the first ~4.5 doublings (6.1-6.8 if Earth triples-quintuples LE capacity by 2045). A 1e6 kg seed cannot hold even one 2026-style leading-edge fab (~3e7 kg of tools).

render_implications.change: Polar factory complexes beside the permanently shadowed ice craters: refineries, fabs and radiator fields lying in the shadowed floors; quarries and the first mass-driver tracks on the night side.
render_implications.numbers: Surface factories allowed until processing heat reaches 5e18 W: model year ~37.

render_implications.change: Only open-pit quarries, beneficiation and equatorial mass-driver tracks remain; pellet streams leave from perihelion.
render_implications.numbers: Mined 7.9e19 kg/yr at the wall; C 1.1e18, Cl 1.1e17, S 1.7e18 kg/yr come up with the rock.

render_implications.change: A dim, edge-on ring of factory radiators along Mercury's orbit: 320 K fab radiators (black in visible, bright in thermal IR) and a smaller 1,000 K refinery fraction glowing dull red; sail packages (14.4 t rolls) departing under ion drive.
render_implications.numbers: Radiator area 1.09e+18 m2 (2026 tech) to 5.75e+18 m2 (2100+): disc-equivalent radius 589000000.0-1350000000.0 m (0.85-2 R_sun), ~1-3 % of the film area made per year.

render_implications.change: Recycling depots co-orbit with the sails; depot craft swap film rolls onto hubs. At any moment ~0.2 % of sails are rolled up or dark for re-skinning.
render_implications.numbers: 6460000.0 refreshes per second at 1 % coverage with L = 10 (2e14 sails per year).

render_implications.change: Mixed generations: newer sails have denser chiplet grids (25.4 -> 19.1 mm pitch), thinner cover glass and sub-bandgap reflecting fronts (brighter in near-IR); ages spread uniformly over 0-10 yr.
render_implications.numbers: Uniform age distribution at steady state; oldest sails show ~8 % PV fade and 1.3 % dead chiplets.

render_implications.change: Exponential to the heat wall (~2096), then a bend toward a ceiling instead of a straight line: B(t) = B_ss - (B_ss - B_cap) exp(-(1-rho)(t-t_cap)/L).
render_implications.numbers: 1 % at model year 62.3; 10 % at 130.0 (2100+ mix) or never (2026 mix) for rho 0.94, L 10.

wildcards.name: Solar-wind hydrogen harvested from the sails
wildcards.detail: The swarm intercepts ~f of the solar wind (~1e9 kg/s in total). Cover glass at 0.92 AU takes 7.46e+20 protons/m2 in 10 yr, above the ~5e16 cm-2 OH saturation of silica, so each m2 holds ~8.37e-07 kg H at retirement. At 1 % coverage with L = 10, remelting old cover glass in vacuum could yield ~174000000000000.0 kg H/yr, about 3.61x Mercury's whole polar-ice H stock every year. That would pay for trace-H passivation and even a-Si:H layers, but not wet processing.

wildcards.name: Atomically precise manufacturing
wildcards.detail: A working nanofactory (10 kg, 1.3 kg/h, 15-h self-duplication) has tool intensity ~1e-4 kg per m2/yr: fabs would vanish as a constraint and J/op could fall below the CMOS floor. But diamondoid mechanosynthesis assumes H-terminated surfaces, so it inherits the hydrogen problem.

wildcards.name: Monolithic logic in the film's own silicon
wildcards.detail: The 20-30 um c-Si absorber is itself crystalline silicon: logic islands patterned into its rear surface would remove 5e15-1.6e16 placements/s and every chip-to-film bond, if the film is single-crystal and web-scale steppers can pattern ~1-3 % of its area.

wildcards.name: Inorganic directed self-assembly
wildcards.detail: If eutectic or oxide self-assembly gives 10-20 nm periods with low defect density on imprinted guides, the panel imprint+DSA class (0.5-10 kg per m2/yr) exists and the growth phase runs at T_d x1.05-1.2 with near-leading-edge chips.

wildcards.name: Fluorine on Mercury
wildcards.detail: MESSENGER never measured F. If F tracks Cl (~0.1 wt%), F-based oxide etch and chamber cleans return and the flow simplifies.

wildcards.name: Shared FEL EUV light
wildcards.detail: One ERL free-electron laser (>10 kW at 13.5 nm) can feed many scanners with no Sn, CO2 laser or H2, and cuts EUV electricity ~3x; it is the natural EUV source for a vacuum fab.

wildcards.name: Self-replicating fabs
wildcards.detail: Over 99.9 % of tool mass (Fe, Si, Mg, Al, glass, ULE-type TiO2-SiO2) is Mercury-native; the "vitamins" (Mo/Ru for EUV mirrors, Sn, In/Ga/As for lasers and sensors, rare-earth magnets) are tiny by mass. The 1980 NASA lunar factory (100 t seed, ~1 yr replication) is the classic closure estimate.

wildcards.name: Core metal after the rock is gone
wildcards.detail: Around calendar ~3100 cumulative delivery reaches the 4e22 kg rock limit; then the fleet decays at (1-rho)/L unless Fe-Ni-Si core metal replaces structure and Si is drawn from the core alloy (3.2e22 kg Si).

Fab tools are treated like any other product mass in the capital balance (optimistic: they are chip-heavy themselves).
